author: fester
body: The Lens platform seam: a Codex-declared function with a real body for the native target is REPLACED at C# emission by a call into a runtime preamble class. The interception rides the two lookups that already fire before any user-definition dispatch. In apply position, emit-apply consults builtin-emitters (is-builtin-name) before the arity map, so a builtin-emitters entry for the seam name rewrites every fully-applied call site. In bare name position, emit-expr-at's IrName case consults lookup-raw-builtin first, so a raw-builtins entry covers the function passed as a value. Both tables match by name alone and therefore shadow user definitions of the same name by construction - that shadowing IS the seam. The native definition's body is skipped at emission (emit-def returns empty for seam names), and the backing preamble class is emitted only when the module actually carries the seam definition (emit-seam- runtimes checks the arity map), so modules that never cite the seam chapter get byte-identical output and no barbarian package dependencies. Current bindings: lens-sql-exec -> _LensSql.exec (Microsoft.Data.SqlClient, connection string from LENS_SQL_CONN); lens-http-next -> _LensHttp.next, lens-http-reply -> _LensHttp.reply, and lens-http-reply-html -> _LensHttp.reply_html (System.Net.HttpListener, one lazily started shared listener per port; the reply flavors differ only in content type). The [LensStore] bindings extend these same tables.

author: fester
body: The IR spells a record field as name/slot - the physical slot index rides behind a slash, exactly as the HTML plug found in CL 6602. cs-field keeps the name, drops the slot, and sanitizes, so emitted member access matches the emitted record declarations. Without the strip every field access renders as a division and the generated C# does not compile; the transpiled-compiler path never noticed because its output is not built by the plug matrix.

author: fester
body: True for a concrete value type - one that can never be a reference to a top-level function. A bare IrName whose type is concrete must be a local (param / let binding), so it is emitted as-is rather than eta-expanded, even when its name collides with a global function of the same name (e.g. a param `ch : IRChapter` vs the Sha256 `ch` of arity 3).
